chunks: From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who bequeathed that Hajj be performed on his behalf for the Hajj of Islam (his obligatory one), and he did not have enough of what he left to cover it except fifty dirhams, he said: 'Hajj shall be performed on his behalf from some of the time periods that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated, from near [the start of the season].'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is applicable to one upon whom Hajj had become obligatory and he did not perform it, then he died and left nothing but fifty dirhams, so it became obligatory to perform Hajj on his behalf with it. And if he had not yet become obligated with the previous Hajj, then he left this amount, it would not be obligatory to perform Hajj on his behalf with it. If he bequeathed that Hajj be performed on his behalf, one-third of what he left is taken out, and Hajj is performed on his behalf with it from the place where he can manage, and that which reveals what we mentioned is what he narrated.

key_terms.خَمْسِينَ دِرْهَمًا: Fifty dirhams (a specific small amount of currency)
key_terms.مِنْ قُرْبٍ: From near (referring to the early part of the Hajj season)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a deceased person left insufficient money to perform their full obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between fulfilling a mandatory Hajj obligation versus a voluntary one when funds are limited, emphasizing that partial performance is valid if the duty was already incumbent. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan’s commentary highlights the jurisprudential nuance that if Hajj was not yet obligatory, the bequest is treated as a standard legacy (one-third of the estate) rather than a direct discharge of debt. This reflects the Shia scholarly focus on precise conditions for *Hajj al-Bada'il* (Hajj of substitution) and the prioritization of obligatory acts over bequests.
